title: Tax the door, not the volume
allegory: A standard SAE is a band paying a noise tax on every notch of volume, so every musician who plays also plays too quietly; a Gated SAE hires a doorman who decides who plays and collects the tax at the door, so the players inside play at true volume.
map: the noise tax on every notch of volume
the L1 sparsity penalty on latent activations
every player turning down to save tax
shrinkage: active latents read systematically low

the gate path: fire or not, carrying the sparsity penalty
players inside playing at true volume
the magnitude path: how strongly, free of the L1 pull

chapters.name: Why so quiet?
chapters.note: every active feature reads a little low...

cap.1: Your sparse autoencoder finds good features, but every active one reads a little low, as if everyone whispered. The penalty for being active is to blame.
cap.2: A standard SAE's L1 penalty pushes all activations towards zero, including the ones that should be large. Active latents come out systematically too small: shrinkage.
cap.3: L1 conflates two decisions: support (which latents fire) and magnitude (how much). Its gradient pulls every active latent down by the same amount, biasing reconstructions low.

cap.1: Picture a band paying a noise tax for every notch of volume. To save tax, whoever plays turns down, even when the song needs them loud.
cap.2: Each latent is one musician. The L1 penalty taxes activation size, so the cheapest solution fires fewer latents and plays each active one quieter than the input deserves.
cap.3: Minimising (a − f)² + λ|f| per latent gives f = max(0, a − λ/2): soft thresholding. Small signals are zeroed, and every survivor is shrunk by λ/2.

cap.1: What each band outputs for a true signal. The taxed band (orange) is always half a notch too quiet. The doorman's band (teal) plays true once inside.
cap.2: Standard SAE ≈ soft threshold: zero below the cut, shrunk by λ/2 above it. Gated SAE ≈ hard threshold: zero below, exact above. Sparsity without the shrinkage.
cap.3: Soft thresholding is the proximal map of the L1 norm; hard thresholding is the L0-style keep-or-kill. The gate implements the latter by moving the penalty off the magnitudes.

cap.1: Split the job. A doorman decides whether each musician plays at all, and the tax is paid at the door. Inside, a separate dial sets the volume.
cap.2: The gate path says fire or not; the magnitude path says how strongly; the latent is their product. The sparsity penalty sits on the gate path, so magnitudes escape it.
cap.3: f = 1[π_gate > 0] ⊙ ReLU(π_mag). The magnitude path reuses the gate's directions with a per-latent rescale; a step has no gradient, so an auxiliary reconstruction loss trains the gate.

chapters.name: Doorman or floor?

right.title: JumpReLU SAE
lines: below it zero, above it exact

chapters.verdict: Same cure for shrinkage; know the idea, then load a pretrained SAE.

cap.1: A cousin design gives each musician a personal volume floor instead of a doorman: below it, silence; above it, true volume. Same cure, different mechanism.
cap.2: Gated SAEs separate gate from magnitude; JumpReLU SAEs use a learned threshold per latent with a straight-through gradient. Both attack shrinkage. GemmaScope's SAEs use JumpReLU.
cap.3: The call: large released dictionaries lean to JumpReLU or TopK; Gated SAEs showed that decoupling works; plain L1 SAEs remain the teaching baseline. You need the shrinkage idea, then a pretrained SAE via SAELens.

chapters.name: Why it matters
items: Better sparsity for the same reconstruction

cap.1: When features read at their true strength, a model's insides are measured honestly. That matters when you use features to explain or steer what a model does.
cap.2: DeepMind showed Gated SAEs beat the standard design on the sparsity/reconstruction frontier. In [1.5.4] you implement one and demonstrate the advantage yourself.
cap.3: Shrinkage biases feature activations and everything built on them: attributions, steering strengths, circuit edges. Unbiased magnitudes make SAE features better instruments for understanding and steering models.

coda.title: Raise the tax: whose volume sags?

caption.1: Drag the tax up and watch the orange line sag below the true line: every active feature reads low. The teal doorman line stays true once through.
caption.2: Both designs zero weak signals below the cut. Above it the standard SAE subtracts λ/2 from everything, while the gated SAE passes the true strength. Only one pays twice for sparsity.
caption.3: Toy per-latent optimum: soft threshold max(0, a − λ/2) versus hard threshold a·1[a > λ/2]. Same support here, but only the soft version biases magnitudes; gating removes the bias.

where_else: JumpReLU SAEs, as in GemmaScope: a learned per-latent threshold, the sibling fix
Lasso regression's shrinkage bias, often fixed by refitting the chosen variables without the penalty
Hurdle models in statistics: one part decides zero or not, another decides how much

hamming.what: A sparse autoencoder whose latents have a gate deciding whether they fire and a separate path deciding how strongly, so the sparsity penalty stops shrinking magnitudes.
hamming.when: When training SAEs where feature strengths matter, and as the conceptual bridge to JumpReLU-style dictionaries.
hamming.why: An L1 penalty on activations biases every active latent low; decoupling firing from magnitude keeps the sparsity without the bias.

object.title: The whisper-free dictionary
object.subtitle: Eight tokens by six latents: tax them for sparsity, then hire the doorman and watch the survivors stand tall.

cap.1: No tax: every latent plays at its true strength, faint ones included. Busy and noisy.
cap.2: λ = 0: activations at full strength, including weak spurious ones.
cap.3: Without a sparsity penalty the code is dense: small activations survive alongside the real features.

cap.1: Add the tax. Faint latents fall silent, which is the point, but every loud one shrinks too.
cap.2: Standard SAE with λ = 1: weak latents zeroed, strong ones all shortened by λ/2.
cap.3: Soft thresholding: correct support, biased magnitudes.

cap.1: Hire the doorman. The same latents stay silent, but the loud ones spring back to full height.
cap.2: Gated at the same λ: identical sparsity pattern, true magnitudes restored.
cap.3: Hard thresholding: same support as the soft version here, with no magnitude bias.

cap.1: Tax harder for extra sparsity and the standard band shrinks further still.
cap.2: Standard SAE at λ = 1.6: more shrinkage on every survivor.
cap.3: Shrinkage grows linearly with λ, so buying sparsity costs reconstruction twice over.

cap.1: The gated band pays for sparsity only at the door. The survivors keep their true height.
cap.2: Gated SAE at λ = 1.6: sparse and unshrunk.
cap.3: Decoupling lets the penalty set support alone, which is why the sparsity/reconstruction frontier improves.

predict.q: Standard SAE with λ/2 = 0.5, true activation 2.0. What does it read?
predict.why: Soft thresholding subtracts λ/2 from every active value.

predict.q: In a Gated SAE, what does the gate decide?

options.t: Whether a latent fires; the magnitude path sets how strongly
How strongly it fires; the magnitude path decides whether

predict.why: Separating the two lets the penalty act on firing without pulling magnitudes down.

predict.q: Gated SAEs and JumpReLU SAEs both target what problem?
predict.why: Both separate 'fire or not' from 'how much': a gate in one, a learned threshold in the other.

object.where: Any time one penalty governs two decisions: split 'whether' from 'how much'.
